name: Mukai Kyorai
bio: 向井去来 (Mukai Kyorai, 1651–1704) was a disciple of Matsuo Bashō and one of the leading poets of his school. He kept a hermitage, the Rakushisha, at Saga near Kyoto, and with Nozawa Bonchō edited the school's anthology Sarumino (1691).
These are the hokku attributed to Kyorai in Basil Hall Chamberlain's study of Bashō and the Japanese epigram (1902), each given in romanised Japanese with Chamberlain's English rendering.

poems.title: Shiri-bito ni
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
Shiri-bito ni
Awaji awaji to
Hana-mi kana

poems.title: Shiri-bito ni (English)
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
No friends, oh! let me meet no friends
When I am gazing at the flowers!

poems.title: Nani-goto zo
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
Nani-goto zo
Hana miru hito no
Naga-gatana

poems.title: Nani-goto zo (English)
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
A sabre! what has such to do
On one who comes to view the flowers?

poems.title: Kokoro naki
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)

poems.title: Kokoro naki (English)
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text: The heartless Government Office,—ay! and the cuckoo.

poems.title: Isogashi ya
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
Isogashi ya
Oki no shigure no
Ma-ho kata-ho

poems.title: Isogashi ya (English)
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
What haste! a shower in the offing,
And sails set straight, and sails set slant.

poems.title: Tsuki-mi sen
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
Tsuki-mi sen
Fushimi no shiro no
Sute-guruwa

poems.title: Tsuki-mi sen (English)
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
I will contemplate from Fushimi's
Abandoned castle-grounds the moon.

poems.title: Yū-gure ya
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
Yū-gure ya
Hage-narabitaru
Kumo no mine

poems.title: Yū-gure ya (English)
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
'Tis evening, and in serried file
Stand the bare pinnacles of cloud.

poems.title: Uki tomo ni
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
Uki tomo ni
Kamarete neko no
Sora nagame

poems.title: Uki tomo ni (English)
poems.author: Mukai Kyorai
poems.collection: Basho and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902)
poems.text:
Bit by a sorry mate, the cat
Intently gazes at the sky.
